Everything you need to profitably scale an ecom brand with Google Ads and YouTube Ads in one tweet:

(Bookmark this.)

📂 Google Ads:

📁 Search Campaigns

- Branded search (exact match)
- Non-branded search (phrase match)
- Competitor search (exact match on brand name)
- Problem-aware search (TOF queries sent to advertorial pages)
- Dynamic search ads (let Google find queries you missed)

📁 Shopping Campaigns

- Branded shopping (exclude non-brand)
- Prospecting shopping (best sellers at low tROAS)
- Testing shopping (new products, separate budget)
- Angle-specific shopping (duplicated listings)

📁 PMax

- Remarketing PMax (HIGH tROAS)
- Feed-only PMax (let product feed cook)
- Full-asset PMax (text, image, video, everything)
- Brand exclusion setup (negative keywords in exact match)
- tROAS split (high on PMax, low on prospecting shopping)

📁 Demand Gen

- Lookalike audiences (customer match upload)
- Custom intent audiences (feed Google the search terms)
- In-market audiences (Google's categorisation of active shoppers)
- Remarketing audiences (video viewers, site visitors, cart abandoners across YouTube)
- Asset group separation (never blend audience types in one asset group)

📂 YouTube Ads

- 6-second bumpers (unskippable)
- 15-second in-stream skippable (MOF warm)
- 30-second in-stream (BOF remarketing, UGC style)
- Shorts ads (vertical 9:16, runs in the Shorts feed, colder ICP)
- Custom intent targeting (people who recently searched your category)
- Placement targeting (ads on specific YouTube videos or channels)

📁 Google Merchant Center

- Title optimisation (brand, product, attributes)
- Description optimisation (5,000 chars of search-relevant keywords)
- Image split testing (lifestyle vs studio, duplicate listings to test, lifestyle wins)
- Sale pricing (struck-through original + green sale price, free conversion rate lift)
- Review feed integration (star ratings on Shopping cards, 2-4 week processing time)
- Feed completeness (GTIN, product type, colour, size, material, custom labels for grouping)
- Regional targeting (separate feeds per country if you sell internationally)
- Shipping accuracy (wrong shipping times = GMC suspension)

📁 Bidding Progression

- 0 conversions: maximise clicks with CPC cap
- ~15 conversions: maximise conversion value
- ~30/month consistent: tROAS (LOW on prospecting)
- Branded campaigns: manual CPC or target impression share, ALWAYS
- Budget scaling: 15-20% every 2-3 days, multi-window analysis (7, 14, 30-day), one KPI

📁 Landing Pages

- Transactional traffic: PDP or collection page, short, product-focused
- Informational traffic: advertorial or editorial, long, education-first
- Comparison traffic: "us vs them" page, credibility-first, objective tone
- Quiz funnel: embedded quiz before PDP, personalised recommendation, 1.5-2.5x conversion rate lift
- Above the fold: headline matching search query, benefit subheadline, result image rather than product image, one CTA button

📁 Ad Copy Framework

- Branded: reasons to buy now, offers, clarity
- Transactional: match the search query, social proof
- Comparison: lead with credibility rather than sales copy
- Informational: lead with education, speak to the research process
- H1 mirrors the search, H2 carries the benefit, H3 carries proof or offer

📁 AI Creative Formats

- Claymation (2-3x CTR, warm tactile aesthetic, beats slop fatigue)
- Pixar-style 3D (premium positioning, high recall, mass-market)
- Balloon world (maximum novelty, crowded market pattern break)
- Musical/singing (highest share rate, TikTok-viral jingles)
- Famous cartoon style (nostalgia activation, family/children products)
- UGC-style AI (social proof, remarketing, hybrid production)
- Cinematic product film (high-ticket justification, brand halo)

📁 AI Tool Stack

- Opus 5 for scripts, prompts, analysis, decisions ($5/$25 per Mtok)
- GPT Images 2.0 for 2K frames (99% text accuracy, agentic reasoning)
- Seedance 2.0 via Higgsfield MCP for animation (native audio, cinematic physics)
- Google Ads MCP (Markifact or Adspirer) for campaign management from Claude

📁 Account Health Signals

- Search Top IS (your rank position vs competitors)
- Search Lost IS by rank (you're being aggressively outbid)
- Search Lost IS by budget (your budget is exhausted before demand is)
- New customer ROAS (the actual prospecting number rather than the blended figure)
- Attribution clarity (branded and non-branded completely separated, always)
- MER (total revenue / total spend, the full-funnel health check)

📁 Funnel Deployment Order

- Phase 1: branded search + branded shopping + non-branded shopping (BOF)
- Phase 2: prospecting shopping + non-branded search + PMax remarketing (MOF)
- Phase 3: Demand Gen + YouTube Ads + TOF search (TOF)
- Always bottom up. Never launch TOF before MOF works.

This is the full map. Every campaign type and format.

The brands printing $100k+ days on Google are pulling from this exact system.

The brands sitting flat at $10k/month are missing 80% of the map.

Continued - THE STRONG MEN WE ARE RAISING

Yesterday’s post sparked quite a few reactions.

And I think one thing needs to be made clear:

This is not an argument against change.

It was never about saying the younger generation is doomed.

If anything, it was meant to make us look beyond the trend, understand the psychology behind it, and question the kind of future we are collectively building.

Let me take it a step further.

I remember being on another space where people were projecting what the next generation would become.

Some said they were genuinely scared.

That the next generation would be worse.
Less disciplined.
Less responsible.
Less connected to reality.
But I remember thinking:

Haven’t people said the same thing about every generation?

I vividly remember my parents talking about their generation with a certain dignity and telling us how different and sometimes disappointing they feared ours would become.

Yet look at what our generation has produced.

Nigeria has produced people who have built companies, technologies and institutions that operate far beyond our borders:

Shola Akinlade & Ezra Olubi built Paystack, which Stripe acquired for more than $200 million.

Iyinoluwa Aboyeji co-founded Andela and Flutterwave and has continued investing in Africa’s next generation of founders.

Olugbenga “GB” Agboola helped build Flutterwave into one of Africa’s most significant payment companies.

Odunayo Eweniyi, alongside her PiggyVest co-founders, helped build one of Nigeria’s most influential savings and investment platforms.

And this isn’t limited to fintech.
We have Nigerian engineers, creators, designers, founders, artists, researchers and builders solving problems that previous generations couldn’t even imagine.

We have young Nigerians building in:

AI
Blockchain
Fintech
Software
Media
Entertainment
Fashion
Education
Creative technology

And even among the younger generation, there are already people proving that the story isn’t simply one of decline.
There are young developers teaching other teenagers to code, young entrepreneurs building businesses, and young Nigerians creating communities around technology and innovation.

So yes, I agree with the “OLODO uprising.”

But I also believe in something else:

THE GENIUS UPRISING.

The builders.

The thinkers.

The disciplined.

The curious.

The ones who understand that going viral is not the same thing as building value.

The ones who understand that money is not the same thing as wealth.

The ones who understand that freedom without responsibility is not progress.

And this is where the conversation becomes personal.

Because the real question isn’t:

“What is wrong with Gen Z?”

The real question is:

“What kind of next generation are YOU raising?”

Because somewhere in the future, your children will become someone else’s leaders.

They will become:

Founders.
Engineers.
Doctors.
Investors.
Policymakers.
Teachers.
Creators.
Parents.
Builders.

And I want to raise children who can look at the world they inherited and say:

“Our parents didn’t fail us.”

I want to raise children who are evidence that despite everything happening around us, we still understood the assignment.

Children who can embrace technology without becoming slaves to it.

Children who can enjoy freedom without abandoning responsibility.

Children who can understand modernity without despising their heritage.

Children who can pursue wealth without losing their values.

Children who can be ambitious without becoming entitled.

Children who can question the world without losing the ability to think.

Because the future isn’t automatically going to be better.

We have to build the people capable of making it better.

And that brings us back to the cycle:

Hard times create strong men. Strong men create good times. Good times create weak men. And weak men create hard times.

Yesterday, I was talking about the cycle.

Today, I’m asking you to look in the mirror.

Are you raising the generation that will break the cycle or continue it?

Because perhaps the future isn’t determined by what Gen Z becomes.

Perhaps it is determined by what we choose to raise.
And that is a much more personal question.

Put that in a box! - Go on - I'll wait...

You can't. And that's exactly the point.

We've been told for so long to pick one thing, niche down, stay in your lane. 

...and for a very specific kind of person - the multi-passionate, the one whose brain lights up in seventeen directions at once - that advice isn't just unhelpful. 

It's actively damaging.

Because you try to pick one thing and it doesn't work. 

Not because you're not disciplined enough - but because you were never built that way. 

You need The Web 🕸️ 

The threads running in multiple directions, each one feeding the others, each one keeping you alive enough to keep going.

But then you beat yourself up for not being able to do the one thing that was never going to work for you anyway.

Stop apologising for being good at things. 

Stop making yourself smaller so other people can understand you more easily. 

That's their job to figure out — not yours to solve for them.

I built a 9-to-5 prison cell in my Core Media years. 

The exact thing I'd spent my whole life refusing to do!

Brick by brick - literally - and called it Ambition.

The relief wasn't leaving. 

The relief was finally admitting I'd built the wrong thing - and that I was the one who could unbuild it.

If it works for you, it works. 

You don't have to justify that to anyone else.

But there's a difference between something working and something quietly killing you while you hustle through it with a smile on. 

Hiding the exhaustion...

Dying slowly in the lane you picked because you thought you were supposed to stay there...

That's not working - That's just very convincing suffering.

The question isn't "does this make sense to other people." 

The question is: 
Does this make sense for me? 
Does it give me energy or drain it? 
Is this the right kind of hard or the wrong kind?

And honestly - that's not even my job to answer for you. 

My job is to help you build the systems, the offers, the content cycles that suits the way YOUR brain and business actually works. 

Which is exactly why I eventually started pulling the charts. 

Because the fastest way to stop fighting yourself is to understand how you're actually wired.

The gates are down - The tools are here. 

Your personal brand is the anchor 

Everything else hangs off it.

Make it beautiful or funny or weird or honest or all of the above.

Just Make It!

Some people are surprised that APIs (aka what Anthropic, OpenAI, and others provide) are treated differently than open weights in the new AI model framework. 

I'm not surprised at all, and it's actually very good policy. Let me explain:

Model weights, APIs, and apps are three very different layers of the stack. Treating them the same would be a recipe for bad regulation.

Think about how we handle cars. We don't regulate steel, we crash-test cars. Nobody asks a steel mill to guarantee that nothing dangerous will ever be built with its steel. Obligations sit with the carmaker and rules of the road with the driver, because that's where risk becomes real and where someone can actually act on it.

Model weights are the steel of AI. They're raw research output, closer to science than product: no user, no interface, no deployment. They don't do anything on their own. And because everything else is built on top of them, this is the layer where regulation does the most damage. Restrict weights and you slow down all progress downstream, and you prevent countless positive use cases from ever emerging: the lab fine-tuning an open model for rare diseases, the startup serving a language big providers ignore, the safety researchers who can only audit models because the weights are open. You don't reduce risk, you just kill open source and concentrate power in a few big labs.

APIs are the middle layer, the parts and engine suppliers of AI: a commercial service where a provider serves a model at scale. Here you have a business relationship, terms of service, the ability to monitor for abuse. It makes sense to expect transparency, security standards, and accountability from providers at this layer, because they can actually enforce things.

Apps are the car on the road: where AI meets the real world. A medical assistant, a hiring tool, a companion for kids, a financial advisor. This is where concrete harm can happen, and conveniently, it's where we already have decades of regulation. Health, finance, employment, consumer protection. An AI hiring tool should comply with employment law whether it's powered by an open model, an API, or a spreadsheet.

The principle is simple: regulate at the layer where risk actually materializes and where actors can act on it. Push obligations to the deployment layer, keep the research layer open. We don't regulate steel, we crash-test cars. Well done @realDonaldTrump @DavidSacks @mkratsios47!

You do the equivalent of submitting it the correct form and it will generate a commercially releasable port based on the idea. One idea is an ADF tri-service fighter that pits characters and vehicles against each other in a bid to drive education, recruitment, veteran community and support. Cheatsheets for all of the good AI models for generating assets with examples. Just read and fill out the form (even better doing this in ChatGPT). Both Android and iPhone distribution via appstores and also web and PWA. Potentially desktop releases depending on the industry stance on AI). Economy is easily added and so is gacha style collection. Is there anything I missed?

I guess I built a game generation platform?

Today, we are announcing Arena's factuality leaderboards, which evaluate the objective performance of AI models in reality and guard against hallucinations.

Arena's chat leaderboard has historically focused on human preference. Although our style control methodology adjusts for the effect of emojis, response length, and other stylistic factors, we wanted a more direct way of measuring objective signals of chatbot utility and anti-hallucination.

Hence, we developed the factuality leaderboards, which speak to the fraction of correct factual claims that a model makes. We basically extract all factual claims and cross-reference them against the internet to ensure they are based in evidence. Models that are supporting their claims with stronger evidence get a better score, and this gives a strong basis for objective performance beyond preference alone.

The big winners, as you can see on this plot, are OpenAI and Grok. Notably, Claude models, as well as Ernie and Muse-Spark-1.1, decrease in ranking.

We're so excited to share this with you! Hope you enjoy!

Update on our robot learning project with @aboraatakan at @uwwatai.

We went from ~30% to 99.8% success on our pick-and-place task by updating our policy from a DINO ViT + transformer policy to a CNN + MLP. Our old model was memorizing the training data and transferring poorly to closed-loop rollouts, so we went the other way and made the model smaller.

The attached video is the CNN + MLP policy running in sim on our async inference stack. We demoed it live for a few hours: 4 failures over 2000+ randomized scenes. This experience has been useful to confirm our stack's correctness. We are now ready to move to hardware!

Next: real hardware, diffusion policy, open-weight fine-tunes, and RL.

Reach out if you're interested in collaborating, and stay tuned.
